originalBugReport.text:
Bug Report: The cart total becomes incorrect or yields NaN/negative values when applying
a discount to an empty cart or when items array is empty.

reproductionEvidence.bugReproducedReason: Test 'empty cart with undefined discount returns 0 (bug: yields NaN)' directly matches the reported symptom. 11 additional tests confirm related defects (negative totals, missing input validation).

failingTests.name: empty cart with undefined discount returns 0 (bug: yields NaN)
decimal result requiring rounding is rounded to 2 dp
discount greater than 100% clamps total to 0 (bug: returns negative)
undefined discountPercentage returns full subtotal (bug: yields NaN)
no discount argument at all returns full subtotal (bug: yields NaN)
negative discount is clamped to 0 (bug: acts as surcharge)
NaN discount throws RangeError (bug: silently produces NaN)
Infinity discount throws RangeError (bug: silently produces -Infinity)
-Infinity discount throws RangeError (bug: silently produces Infinity)
item with undefined price throws TypeError (bug: silently accumulates NaN)
item with missing price property throws TypeError (bug: silently accumulates NaN)
item with negative price throws TypeError (bug: silently accepts)

passingTestsInRedRun: empty cart with no discount returns 0
empty cart with a non-zero discount returns 0 (bug: may yield NaN or negative)
normal items with 0% discount returns full subtotal
normal items with 10% discount returns correct discounted total
decimal amounts are rounded to 2 decimal places

defects.description: When discountPercentage is undefined, the expression subtotal * undefined evaluates to NaN, propagating through the calculation and returning NaN.
When discountPercentage > 100, discount > subtotal, so subtotal - discount is negative. No clamp is applied.
No guards for NaN, ±Infinity, undefined discount, or missing/non-numeric/negative item prices. All silently propagate through arithmetic.

testResults.name: extreme discount (200%) never returns a negative total
discount above 100% returns 0, not a negative number
undefined discount is treated as 0% (full price returned)
missing discount argument is treated as 0%
negative discount is clamped to 0% (no surcharge)
item with undefined price throws TypeError
item with missing price property throws TypeError
item with negative price throws TypeError
floating-point prices are rounded to 2 decimal places
discount on decimal prices rounds to 2dp

changedFiles.reason: Written by the Test Agent with 18 regression tests targeting the reported bug and all agreed business rules.

Patched by the Fix Agent after diff approval: NaN/Infinity guard (Rule 6), undefined/null normalisation (Rule 4), negative clamp (Rule 5), empty-cart early return (Rule 3), per-item price validation (Rules 7 & 8), total clamp ≥ 0 (Rule 2), 2dp rounding (Rule 9).

remainingLimitations.description: Rule 1 (subtotals calculated from item prices) has no dedicated test asserting it in isolation; it is only implicitly exercised by discount tests.
Items array containing null or non-object entries (e.g. [null, {price:10}]) will throw an uncontrolled runtime TypeError rather than a meaningful guarded one.
discountPercentage passed as a numeric string (e.g. '10') bypasses the NaN/Infinity guard (typeof check) and relies on JS implicit coercion. No test documents this behavior.
Item prices that are numeric-looking strings (e.g. { price: '10' }) correctly throw TypeError due to the typeof check, but no test documents this expectation.
